text:
eli: Heads up — after the kernel-routing tweak landed at 06:12 UTC the token-level p95/p99 spiked for short sequences on Dedicated pools. Metrics look weirdly sparse from the runtime exporters too.

sara: saw that, noticed a bunch of missing statsd counters around 06:12-06:14. Could be exporter churn? :thinking_face:

dan: confirmed. Grafana shows a sharp drop in `runtime.tokens.emitted` for ~2m and then a jump. Traces show the requests used TRT fallback for some shards.

minh: that timing matches my deploy (kernel-selection heuristics changed to prefer TRT for seq_len<=64 when memory pressure low). I didn't expect exporter churn.

perf-eng: can you paste the profiler output? want to rule out kernel-side queueing.

eli: profiler snippet (from dev cluster):
```
[2025-11-03T06:12:45Z] sample: batch_size=8 seq=32 kernel_choice=trt latency_ms=6.2
[2025-11-03T06:12:45Z] sample: batch_size=1 seq=8 kernel_choice=cuda latency_ms=14.1
[2025-11-03T06:12:46Z] kernel_switches=214 kv_cache_hits=0.12 kv_cache_misses=0.88
```

sara: kv_cache_hits that low for short seqs is suspicious — we should still have prefix caching for most routes. Maybe cache key computation changed?

dan: also seeing weird batching: batching heuristics pushed a lot of small batches through TRT which reduces amortized token work but increases per-token latency for 1-2 token responses.

minh: ugh, yes — the heuristic had a bug where `prefer_trt_for_short` ignored `cache_prefetch` flag. So TRT got cold KV cache a lot and we lost prefix reuse.

perf-eng: that explains both latency and low kv hits. But what about the exporter drops? infra-bot shows OTLP exporter restarted around the same minute.

infra-bot: deploy-bot triggered rolling-restart of runtime-exporter (v1.3.7 -> v1.3.8) at 2025-11-03T06:11:58Z for security patch. All pods restarted over ~90s. Some metrics buffered, others dropped.

ops: so two orthogonal things: kernel-routing bug causing cold cache + exporter rolling restart causing gaps. Both line up with spike.

eli: agree. immediate plan: revert the `prefer_trt_for_short` change (minh), run a targeted backfill for dropped metrics (ops), and run a perf regression job on dedicated cluster to validate.

minh: reverting now, will roll back the heuristic flag in canary. :eye:

dan: ops — can you run a backfill for 06:09-06:16 window? use StatsD raw logs if available, otherwise backfill from OTLP fallback. We need token-level breakdowns restored.

ops: scheduling backfill job now. note: two paths — quick partial backfill from buffered exporter files (faster, lossy) or full backfill using raw request logs (slower, exact). Which do you want?

eli: start with buffered exporter files to get dashboards coherent, then full backfill overnight to ensure alerting baselines are accurate.

perf-eng: I'll run the perf regression harness against the canary after rollback. Also adding a microbenchmark that simulates cold KV cache + small-batch TRT to reproduce.

minh: rollback complete on canary (06:18). will promote if canary stays green for 10m.

infra-bot: backfill job created: backfill-1763500000-1 (buffered-exporter) triggered at 06:23 UTC. owner=ops.

dan: quick note for dashboards — add an annotation over the spike window explaining both exporter restart and heuristic change so oncall doesn't chase the wrong root cause later.

ops: added grafana annotation and slack alert note. starting full raw-log backfill at 23:00 UTC.

eli: follow-ups: 1) add unit test to prevent ignoring `cache_prefetch` in kernel routing (minh), 2) change exporter restart playbook to do staggered restarts with grace for buffered metrics (infra), 3) create a token-latency dashboard panel split by kernel_choice + kv_cache_hit for per-route KPIs (perf-eng).

minh: filing PR for the unit test now.

perf-eng: I'll own the dashboard panel and add anomaly alerts tied to backfilled baselines.

ops: backfill completed (buffered) at 06:29 — dashboards updated. full raw-log backfill started as scheduled.

eli: thanks all — let's keep an eye on p99 while full backfill runs. If anything else pops up, ping here. :thumbsup:
